programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha an latha fìor theth ‘s tha Bing ‘s Flop a ceannach reòiteag son iad fhèin a chumail fionnar. Ge-tà, mus faigh iad air na reòiteagan ithe, tha aoidh annasach a nochdadh a tha feumach air beagan taic bhuapa...! It’s a very hot day and Bing and Flop have bought themselves ice lollies to help keep them cool. However, an unexpected guest in need of some help distracts them from their treats before they manage to eat them!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Abair g’ eil deagh spòrs a’ dol ‘s Bing ‘s Sula a’ peantadh dealbh-balla còmhla. Ge-tà, tha trioblaid ag èirigh nuair a thig dathan bhon dealbh aig Bing am measg an dealbh a tha Sula air a chruthachadh...! Great fun is had at Ama’s crèche as Bing and Sula create their own mural. However, things get a bit fraught when paint from Bing’s rainbow picture runs into the tree that Sula was carefully creating!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha Ben agus na h-Abadas a' cluich an geama fhaclan 's Ben ag iarraidh orra bara-cuibhle a lorg. Tha Hari, Seren 's Ella uile den bheachd gun tig aca air am facal ùr a lorg ach cò thig a thaghadh an-diugh? Ben plays the word game with the Abadas and sends them on a search for a wheelbarrow. Hari, Seren and Ela all believe they can find out the meaning of the word, but who will go on the adventure?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Nìp ga lorg fhèin ann an suidheachadh steigeach às dèidh a bhith a’ feuchainn air cleasan siorcais. Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh a’ cuideachadh Nìp ga ghlanadh fhèin, ach chan eil an seo ach toiseach nan trioblaidean aige. Neep gets himself into a sticky situation, copying tricks from the circus. Abney and Teal help him to get cleaned up, but that's only the start of his problems!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha màthair Pheicein a’ trod ris às dèidh dha a ràdh ri nurs gu bheil a sròn mòr. Bhon mhionaid sin, tha Peicein a’ tòiseachadh ri breugan beaga innse, is tha iad sin a’ sìor fhàs nam breugan mòra, is ag adhbharrachadh mì-thuigse uabhasach! Petit's mum scolds him for telling a nurse that she has a big nose. From that moment on, Petit starts telling white lies that grow little by little, until they turn into big lies and cause a huge misunderstanding.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Abigail NicÌomhair a’ leughadh Balach anns na Sgòthan. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Greg Stobbs agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Abigail Maciver reads Balach anns na Sgòthan, written and illustrated by Greg Stobbs and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Dè tha Alpheus Benthos ris an-diugh? As bith dè, chan eil smachd aige air gnothaichean! What is Alpheus Benthos up to today? Whatever it is, he has no control over things!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an taigh ri sgeadachadh ach tha Bitzer feumach air taic nuair tha e air fhàgail os cionn ghnothaichean. Ach 's e barrachd bacadh tha e a' faighinn bhon threud seach cuideachadh - abair bùrach! When the farmer pops out for more supplies, Bitzer is left in charge of decorating and calls on the flock for help. He soon realises this may be a terrible mistake, as they have their own way of doing things - painting and decorating isn't their strong point!

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl a’ cruthachadh piñata ann an cumadh crosgaig do cho-là-breith Chailein. Ach tha e a’ cur dragh uabhasach air Cailean nuair a tha na Pluic a’ tòiseachadh ri bhualadh. Tha Cailean deimhinne nach toil le Pòl e tuilleadh, is tha e a’ fàgail an dachaigh is a’ tilleadh gu muir. An lorg Pòl Cailean airson innse dha gu bheil e fada ceàrr? Dave makes a Gareth-shaped piñata for Gareth’s birthday, but his starfish friend is confused when the Spuds bash it to pieces. Convinced that Dave does not like her anymore, Gareth leaves and heads out to sea. Can Dave find her in time and persuade her that it was all a silly misunderstanding?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha an sgoil a’ cur Pòl air greis-gnìomhnachais còmhla ri athair aig an dump. An sin tha Pòl ag ionnsachadh tòrr mu sgudal, is tha seann dèideag de bhò agus fridsichean neo-rianail a’ toirt air smaoineachadh mu dheidhinn ath-chuairteachadh. School puts Dave on a work placement with his dad at the local dump. Sucked into the mysterious world of rubbish, an old cow and a group of unruly fridges teach Dave a lesson about recycling.

programme.title: Eilean Mo Ghaoil (From Lewis with Love)
programme.desc: Peigi Ann is busy with lambing, the west side football team are on home ground for an important game and Mairi and Tom take home the peats.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Abi Reid from Stirlingshire is Joy's guest, and Calum Maclean is in Islay visiting a distillery.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Dealbhan Fraoich/Heather's Portraits
programme.desc: Heather travels to South Uist where she meets Father Colin MacInnes. A priest for over 50 years, Father Colin spent over three decades working among the people of Ecuador. There he helped transform a hillside shanty town on the outskirts of Quito into a thriving community with a hospital, banks, schools and churches. Tha Fraoch Nic an Deòir a Ìle air ais air an sgrion le sreath ùr de “Dhealbhan Fraoich”. An dà chuid na tè-ealain agus na ceasnaiche, tha i a’dèanamh dealbhan dathte de Ghàidheil air a bheil sinn eòlach – agus a’tàladh asta iomadh sgeul mu eachdraidh am beatha. Sa phrògram seo, tha Fraoch a’siubhal a dh’Uibhist a Deas gus coinneachadh ri Maighstir Cailean MacAonghais. Tha esan air a bhi na shagart fad còrr is lethcheud bliadhna. Chuir e seachad barrachd air deich bliadhna fichead ag obair còmhla ri muinntir Ecuador: gu ìre is gun do chuidich e gus coimhearsnachd thruagh aig oir prìomh bhaile Quito a thoirt air adhart gu bhi na àite soirbheachail le ospadal, sgoiltean, eaglaisean is bancaichean. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha dubhadh na grèine a’ cur sgleò air a’ Chamas agus air fortan nan sgiobair – tha iad a’ ruith a-mach à connadh, tha na clèibh aotrom agus chan eil càil a’ gabhail mar bu chòir. A solar eclipse darkens the Gulf and the captains’ fortunes - fuel is low, traps are light, and nothing’s biting like it should. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Katie MacRitchie from Harris joins Angus Mackay to go fishing on a moody, misty summer's morning off the east coast of Lewis. Watched closely by a golden eagle, they fish for mackerel as the sun gradually emerges and chat about the role that fishing plays in the community life of the islands. Tha Katie NicRisnidh às na Hearadh còmhla ri Aonghas MacAoidh agus iad ag iasgach air madainn shamhraidh ghruamach, cheòthach far costa an ear Leòdhais. Tha iad ag iasgach airson rionnach, le iolaire-bhuidhe gan coimhead, fhad ’s a nochdas a’ ghrian mean air mhean agus iad a’ bruidhinn mun àite a th’ aig iasgach ann am beatha coimhearsnachd nan h-eileanan.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Tha tairgse tharraingeach air tighinn bho Lewis Friseal. Feumaidh a’ chlann-nighean còmhradh mu bhith a’ reic a’ ghnothachais ach aig an dearbh àm seo chan eil iad a’ bruidhinn ri chèile. Tha sùil Katie air mogan airgid. Tha Angela a’ bruadar mu ghaol fad-astarach. Tha Daniel a’ cur seachad a shaoghal aig obair far a a bheil peinnseanairean le eòlas a’ tabhann comhairle àraid. Tha Betty a’ nochdadh dreach ùr, dàn airson sèisean coimhead nan eun. An dàrna sreath den chomadaidh magaidh-aithriseach le Hannah McKirdy agus Lana Pheutan mar chleasaichean agus sgrìobhaichean. A tempting offer from Lewis Fraser is on the table. The girls need to discuss selling the business, but right now they aren’t speaking to each other. Katie sees pound signs. Angela’s dreaming of long-distance love. Daniel spends all his time at work, where some experienced OAPs offer some choice romance advice. Betty unveils a bold new look for birdwatching season. Series two of the popular mockumentary comedy written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Sar Sgeoil
programme.desc: Se leabhar clasaigeach Canadach le deagh bhlas Albannach a th’anns an leabhar Anne of Green Gables. Tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a’ sealltainn cho buileach Gàidhealach sa bha coimhearsnach Eilean a’ Phrionnsa, àite-breith is fuirich an ùghdair, Lucy Maud NicGumaraid. Rugadh i air Là Naomh Anndra, 1874. ‘S ann air a làithean-àraich aonranach gun ghaol a steidhich i tè de prìomh charactaran ann an saoghal ficsean, Anne Shirley. Tha an sgeulachd bhlàth seo air tighinn tro na lìnntinn agus air a h-eadar-theangachadh ann an ceathrad diofar cànan, Gàidhlig na luib. Anne of Green Gables is a classic Canadian novel, with a strong Scottish accent. Cathy MacDonald reveals that Prince Edward Island, where Lucy Maud Montgomery was born and wrote her internationally acclaimed novel, was a distinctly Scottish community. Born on St Andrews Day (30th November) 1874, Montgomery had an unhappy childhood during which she felt unloved. But she used the experience to create one of fiction’s best loved characters - Anne Shirley. The heartwarming tale is an enduring classic that has been translated in almost 40 languages, including Gaelic. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Featuring musical stars Mike McGoldrick, Aly Bain, Jerry Douglas, Aoife O’ Donovan and Mary Chapin Carpenter.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater Robbie Cumming begins his 170-mile journey across the north of England and soon runs into difficulty when he encounters a problem with his craft's propeller in Wigan and runs aground in Blackburn. Nevertheless, he pushes on to navigate a true wonder of the waterways, the Burnley Embankment.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a spectacular close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. He also visits the magnificent Elizabethan mansion of Longleat, seat of the Marquesses of Bath, to find out about the estate’s remarkable survival after the Second World War. At Chippenham in Wiltshire, Michael pays a call on a signalling manufacturer that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades and has a go on the centre’s simulator, driving the Elizabeth Line train to Paddington.

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: It’s the ultimate question: why are we here? Brian Cox explores how cutting-edge space missions take us back 13.8 billion years to the origin of the universe.

programme.title: This is BBC Four
programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm.

programme.title: This is BBC Four
programme.desc: Daily from 7.00pm.

programme.title: This is BBC Four

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches England’s south coast to continue his exploration of postwar Britain. He begins in Dorset on the Swanage Railway, riding a glorious 1940s steam locomotive on the trail of one of Britain’s most popular children’s authors, Enid Blyton. In Poole, Michael discovers an icon of the Swinging Sixties – the lava lamp, invented in the town by an eccentric accountant. At Romsey, Michael heads to the magnificent Broadlands Estate, once home of Louis Mountbatten, first Earl Mountbatten of Burma. Michael’s last stop on this leg of the journey is Portchester, on the northern edge of Portsmouth Harbour, where he visits a factory manufacturing a marine craft pioneered in the 1950s – the hovercraft.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater and film-maker Robbie Cumming crosses the Pennines on the picturesque Leeds and Liverpool Canal, and lends a hand to hire boaters in Gargrave, North Yorkshire. He also encounters Bingley Five Rise Locks, a wonder of the inland waterways.

programme.title: Gods and Monsters: Homer's Odyssey
programme.desc: Virginia Woolf said that Homer's epic poem the Odyssey was 'alive to every tremor and gleam of existence'. Following the magical and strange adventures of warrior king Odysseus, inventor of the idea of the Trojan horse, the poem can claim to be the greatest story ever told. Now British poet Simon Armitage goes on his own Greek adventure, following in the footsteps of one of his own personal heroes. Yet Simon ponders the question of whether he even likes the guy.

programme.title: Bletchley Park: Codebreaking's Forgotten Genius
programme.desc: Documentary looking at Gordon Welchman, a codebreaker crucial to the allies defeating the Nazis in World War II. Filmed extensively at Bletchley Park.

programme.title: Blade Runner
programme.desc: Ridley Scott's sci-fi classic. Los Angeles, 2019. Mankind has succeeded in creating replicants - near-perfect humanoids superior in intelligence even to humans - but as a result of a mutiny on a human colony in outer space, it is now illegal for unlicensed replicants to be on Earth. The punishment, if they are caught, is death. Four replicants have escaped and fled back to Earth, and android hunter or 'blade runner' Deckard is charged with identifying and 'retiring' them...

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Charlotte Bronte's classic about an orphan girl who grows up to become a governess in a gloomy manor in Yorkshire, where she falls in love with the mysterious Edward Rochester.

programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a spectacular close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. He also visits the magnificent Elizabethan mansion of Longleat, seat of the Marquesses of Bath, to find out about the estate’s remarkable survival after the Second World War. At Chippenham in Wiltshire, Michael pays a call on a signalling manufacturer that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades and has a go on the centre’s simulator, driving the Elizabeth Line train to Paddington.

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: It’s the ultimate question: why are we here? Brian Cox explores how cutting-edge space missions take us back 13.8 billion years to the origin of the universe.

programme.title: This is BBC Four

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches England’s south coast to continue his exploration of postwar Britain. He begins in Dorset on the Swanage Railway, riding a glorious 1940s steam locomotive on the trail of one of Britain’s most popular children’s authors, Enid Blyton. In Poole, Michael discovers an icon of the Swinging Sixties – the lava lamp, invented in the town by an eccentric accountant. At Romsey, Michael heads to the magnificent Broadlands Estate, once home of Louis Mountbatten, first Earl Mountbatten of Burma. Michael’s last stop on this leg of the journey is Portchester, on the northern edge of Portsmouth Harbour, where he visits a factory manufacturing a marine craft pioneered in the 1950s – the hovercraft.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater and film-maker Robbie Cumming crosses the Pennines on the picturesque Leeds and Liverpool Canal, and lends a hand to hire boaters in Gargrave, North Yorkshire. He also encounters Bingley Five Rise Locks, a wonder of the inland waterways.

programme.title: Gods and Monsters: Homer's Odyssey
programme.desc: Virginia Woolf said that Homer's epic poem the Odyssey was 'alive to every tremor and gleam of existence'. Following the magical and strange adventures of warrior king Odysseus, inventor of the idea of the Trojan horse, the poem can claim to be the greatest story ever told. Now British poet Simon Armitage goes on his own Greek adventure, following in the footsteps of one of his own personal heroes. Yet Simon ponders the question of whether he even likes the guy.

programme.title: Bletchley Park: Codebreaking's Forgotten Genius
programme.desc: Documentary looking at Gordon Welchman, a codebreaker crucial to the allies defeating the Nazis in World War II. Filmed extensively at Bletchley Park.

programme.title: Blade Runner
programme.desc: Ridley Scott's sci-fi classic. Los Angeles, 2019. Mankind has succeeded in creating replicants - near-perfect humanoids superior in intelligence even to humans - but as a result of a mutiny on a human colony in outer space, it is now illegal for unlicensed replicants to be on Earth. The punishment, if they are caught, is death. Four replicants have escaped and fled back to Earth, and android hunter or 'blade runner' Deckard is charged with identifying and 'retiring' them...

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Charlotte Bronte's classic about an orphan girl who grows up to become a governess in a gloomy manor in Yorkshire, where she falls in love with the mysterious Edward Rochester.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The race between America and China to lead the world in artificial intelligence is reshaping the global balance of power. But behind the headlines, a hidden conflict is unfolding. Join AI Decoded as we examine the seizure of $13 million worth of advanced AI chips allegedly bound for China, and Anthropic's claim that Alibaba carried out the largest known AI 'distillation attack' in history. As nations and tech giants compete for supremacy, the battle for AI is increasingly being fought in the shadows. Who will win the race for AI dominance, and how far will they go to get there?

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: Paul follows the River Ayr as it flows from Loch Glenbuck towards the sea and the Clyde coast. The old mining village of Glenbuck was demolished long ago, but its memory is kept alive by former resident Barbara Alexander whose uncle, the famous Liverpool football manager Bill Shankly, was a Glenbuck man. From Glenbuck, Paul follows the river through a landscape pockmarked by the scars of old mineral extraction and industry. At Muirkirk he discovers how a local man illuminated the cities of the world with gas lighting, and how a certain Mr McAdam invented tarmac for the roads of the world. The course of the river Ayr flows through land rich in covenanting history when religious conflict cost many lives. In the Ayr gorge, Paul encounters the extraordinary tale of the radical preacher Alexander Peden, whose life on the run forced him to hide in caves while still preaching hellfire sermons to the people. Finally reaching the coast, Paul visits the only working salt evaporation tower in the world. Here, with a pinch of salt, he learns how sea water is evaporated by wind and sun to make brine, from which sea salt is made.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Calum Clunie are back together to tackle the week’s jobs at Beechgrove Garden. Although George got a special picking of potatoes for his birthday in June, this is the time to lift the first crop from the vegetable plot and try out this year’s produce. Calum and George check on the brassicas that were planted in the club root-infected bed, testing varieties that are said to be resistant to the infection. George is back to work on the privet hedge that was given a severe pruning last year to encourage thicker growth, Calum gets round to placing plants known for their fragrance in his competition bed, and there are the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers and Grado uncover the best holiday escapes in Scotland. However, it’s up to friends and families from all over Scotland to decide which escapes make it to the grand final. Scotland’s greatest campsite, caravan or chalet escape is decided by the Browns, a fun-loving family of four from central Scotland. With two kids under ten to entertain, how will they rate a night in the treehouses at Lanrick, a secluded, hand-crafted cabin at Arcadia Glamping and a campsite on a remote Hebridean island?

programme.title: Confessions of a Teenage Fraudster
programme.desc: Facing deportation to the UK, it seems inevitable that Elliot will fall into the hands of British cops who have put together an extensive case of his crimes. Once again, though, he has other ideas. After four years of travelling the world spending fraudulently accrued money, he continues to be chased by investigators and cops. In truth, the one thing Elliot desires as much as freedom is a settled life. But even when he thinks he’s found it, with a new home and friends, there is no escape from his trail of lies and deception. Eventually, with his life unravelling, his spending becoming chaotic and a growing resentment for the fraud that has funded his lifestyle, justice catches up with Elliot.

programme.title: Growing Up Scottish
programme.desc: Some of Scotland's favourite comedians and entertainers remember Scottish weddings, from stags and hens to speeches, group photos and ceilidh dancing.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Thrills, spills and lengthy lunch bills as the bold Bravehearts flash the blue light and curtail criminality. Traffic officer Hugh McKirdy regrets going commando - his partner Surjit Singh dutifully provides cover while he seeks reinforcement undergarments. At Coms HQ, there's a promotion for Maggie Le Beau, but the new call centre team leader soon discovers a breakdown in communications. Retired Police Chief Sir Neville Archibald selects the swankiest of eateries for an elongated procedural discussion with Cameron Miekelson. The local cop shop becomes a hotbed of political activity as officer Karen encounters an unstoppable force of passion. Cop comedy cuffing crime in all its guises. Starring Jack Docherty, Grado, Manjot Sumal, ML Stone, Karen Bartke, Darren Connell, Paul Sneddon and special guest Bill Paterson.

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: It turns out that Janey and Ashley fight every time they are together on a flight - so will sparks fly as they try out three very different jobs in an airport? Customer service, attention to detail and following instructions are essential when checking people in, baggage handling and working as part of the airport’s fire service. However, there is a lot to remember and absolutely no room for error, not to mention the challenge of fighting a fire on a fuselage. Can Ashley and Janey impress their boss and keep to the schedule? And which one will win the ‘best employee’ trophy?

programme.title: Selling Scotland
programme.desc: Jack Docherty takes an entertaining look at Scotland's most memorable adverts. Joining him on this archive journey will be some of Scotland's funniest and best known faces.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: The action shifts to Steve's home turf as the Deadly 60 team scour the UK in search of its lethal beauties. From the wild seas off the Pembrokeshire coast to the New Forest, Steve proves that British wildlife is anything but boring. Gannets prove to be more than a match for Steve in a diving competition. He battles with the elements to reach the birds but the rough seas are determined to stop him. He then has to confront his past as he comes face to face with the only venomous snake that has hospitalised him. The Deadly team also have a close call as they uncover a hornets' nest in a loft, and Steve gets a taste of what it is like to be prey for a day as he is hunted through a forest by a hungry goshawk.

Meanwhile, back in the UK Jeremy tests the feisty new Fiat 500 Abarth and pop idol Will Young is the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay keeps the questions coming as the week hits its midpoint. TV presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic gold medallist Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook are back for more as the quiz pulls into Paisley, shining a light on the town’s history and hidden gems. Paul Gorton resumes his role as uncertified tour guide, blending unbelievable facts with playfully planted untruths as the overall leaderboard continues to take shape.

programme.title: What Happened at...?
programme.desc: On 1 July 1916, nearly 20,000 British soldiers were killed on the first day of the Battle of the Somme – one of the bloodiest days in the history of warfare and a lasting symbol of both sacrifice and futility. In this documentary, Jordan Dunbar examines how communities have been shaped by the battle and reveals how its legacy continues to resonate through families - including his own.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Joe Swash goes in search of his Italian roots. Along the way, he finds stories of murder, banditry, an inspiring political activist and a family bar in southern Italy.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A voice analyst makes a positive link to the killer of two police officers, and a lead forensic scientist identifies a phone snatcher from a shoe he left behind.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As Adam Frost’s brand new garden starts to take shape, it’s time to get some shrubs in the ground and construct a path. He also makes a start on planting up a potted herb garden and shares some ideas on what to grow against a wall, whether it be sunny or shady. At home in Devon, Carol Klein is mixing it up with flowers and edibles, where sweet peas and cosmos happily mingle with beetroot, basil and beans. And at West Dean Gardens in Chichester, Jamie Butterworth reveals the secrets of growing that border belle, the delphinium. In Birmingham, a lover of roses has created a garden full to brimming with beautiful blooms, while a gardener in Norwich shares her contemporary cottage garden that became a refuge when she needed it most.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: On this Grand Tour, Paul explores the lower reaches of Royal Deeside. Heading downstream, he runs aground in a canoe and then gets stuck trying to thread his body through an ancient fertility stone. In the village of Banchory, he breathes in the scent of lavender, and then takes a train along the Royal Deeside Line before heading into Aberdeen where he learns a secret recipe for the city’s famous rowie - a Caledonian version of the croissant. Journey’s end is on the city’s famous golden sands.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: At home in the Yorkshire Dales, Emmerdale stars and best mates Matthew Wolfenden and Roxy Shahidi take on the Antiques Road Trip challenge. Rolling in a retro Riley sports saloon, they're romping around the rolling hills in search of antique bargains. Paired up with super-fan Hettie Jago and legend of the game Steven Moore, they embark on a battle of the paperweights. And the competition steps up a gear when our feisty foursome find themselves around an original Monopoly board. Who's going to get the boot?

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: A ten-year-old boy is swept out to sea on a paddleboard in North Berwick. His parents have rushed out to try and save him, but all three of them are now struggling in the water. In Walmer, a yacht has run aground on the notorious Goodwin Sands. It’s a race against time to get the three casualties onto the safety of the lifeboat. On the Sussex coast, an urgent call has come in for two men trapped by the incoming tide beneath cliffs four miles east of Newhaven. And on the banks of the River Thames in London, the Teddington crew get more than they bargained for when they come to the aid of an injured cyclist - who just happens to be a former Blue Peter presenter.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Webster, the famous barrister, is not well and not an easy man to look after. His carer Urban knows how to take the rough with the smooth, dishing out the drugs or appealing to the old man’s vanity. But on this particular night, something is coming that will test Webster’s resolve and legal skills to the very end.

programme.title: To Think Like a Killer
programme.desc: When the FBI calls, Dr Ann Burgess joins a new task force hunting serial predators and is thrust into an active investigation involving the assault of over 20 women.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay keeps the questions coming as the week hits its midpoint. Paul Gorton resumes his role as uncertified tour guide, blending unbelievable facts with playfully planted untruths as the overall leaderboard continues to take shape.

programme.title: What Happened at...?
programme.desc: On 1 July 1916, nearly 20,000 British soldiers were killed on the first day of the Battle of the Somme – one of the bloodiest days in the history of warfare and a lasting symbol of both sacrifice and futility. In this documentary, Jordan Dunbar examines how communities have been shaped by the battle and reveals how its legacy continues to resonate through families - including his own.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Joe Swash goes in search of his Italian roots. Along the way, he finds stories of murder, banditry, an inspiring political activist and a family bar in southern Italy.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As Adam Frost’s brand new garden starts to take shape, it’s time to get some shrubs in the ground and construct a path. He also makes a start on planting up a potted herb garden and shares some ideas on what to grow against a wall, whether it be sunny or shady. At home in Devon, Carol Klein is mixing it up with flowers and edibles, where sweet peas and cosmos happily mingle with beetroot, basil and beans. And at West Dean Gardens in Chichester, Jamie Butterworth reveals the secrets of growing that border belle, the delphinium. In Birmingham, a lover of roses has created a garden full to brimming with beautiful blooms, while a gardener in Norwich shares her contemporary cottage garden that became a refuge when she needed it most.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: On this Grand Tour, Paul explores the lower reaches of Royal Deeside. Heading downstream, he runs aground in a canoe and then gets stuck trying to thread his body through an ancient fertility stone. programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: A ten-year-old boy is swept out to sea on a paddleboard in North Berwick. His parents have rushed out to try and save him, but all three of them are now struggling in the water. In Walmer, a yacht has run aground on the notorious Goodwin Sands. It’s a race against time to get the three casualties onto the safety of the lifeboat. On the Sussex coast, an urgent call has come in for two men trapped by the incoming tide beneath cliffs four miles east of Newhaven. And on the banks of the River Thames in London, the Teddington crew get more than they bargained for when they come to the aid of an injured cyclist - who just happens to be a former Blue Peter presenter.

programme.desc: Weasy makes fun of the Ducklings for playing with a doll they found in the farmer's yard, but in reality, Weasy wants to play too! When it goes missing, the Ducklings must trick him to get it back.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: The town’s ferris wheel is stuck, so Mojo and Bo have to get it moving. But they do their job too well, because the wheel rolls away, forcing Mojo and Bo to chase it down.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum and Dad vow to only finish their boring housework when the kids stop acting silly!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The kids are late for a playdate, but they can’t leave before they finish their game.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: After 799 years of winning the Great Gnome Games, Great Gnanna is worried she can't defend her title. To help, the doctors remind her that she is just as fearsome as ever.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Theo believes aliens are coming to the Den for a game of space football and attempts to recruit the others. Meanwhile, Fern has persuaded the adults to form a band.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Waffle's last day at the Brooklyn-Bells' but he still finds time to upset neighbour Mrs Hobbs. Simon hears Waffle speak. Will he finally agree that the family can keep the special dog?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi promises her dads she will go straight to bed while Aunty T babysits. But when Aunty T suggests night-time ice cream, Rafi makes a wish and her bed magically flies them out into Manchester! It’s exciting at first, but soon Rafi becomes sleepy and wants to go home. Suddenly, the wish runs out and the bed drops onto a tree. Luckily, Aunty T uses her umbrella to magic them safely back. Rafi realises bedtime is bedtime for a reason.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran have a barbecue with their extended family, including Mummy, Daddy, Great-Gran Gran, Auntie Dee, Uncle Tyrell and Cousin Lexi. JoJo and Lexi prepare a dance, but Lexi’s portable speaker runs out of battery, so they dance to an old school song on Gran Gran’s record player instead.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Whilst at the Big Shop, Sarah, Duck and Plate Girl discover some unusual inhabitants in the plant section.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny and Small find a box that has fallen from space. It contains just two circles of black cloth, but these are no ordinary circles - they are holes, and one leads to another. Tiny and Small are very excited and try to tell Major about their discovery, but he is too busy to listen and so they decide to do their own experiments, with quite amazing results.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa water a flower and give some thirsty Tweeties a drink too. At Play Time, they play with a present wrapped in flower petals and take turns unwrapping it, revealing a new layer of petal wrapping each time. At Yummy Time, they use petals as napkins. They bring the present to the Bay of Books, where they remove the final wrapping and reveal a wonderful surprise just in time for Storytime.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Tombliboos explore inside their house. It is full of interesting spaces, stairs to climb and slides to slide down. They go right to the top of their house, each one higher than the next, but down below Makka Pakka is waiting to wash their faces so they must come all the way down again.

programme.desc: Lively sitcom. programme.title: Piglets
programme.desc: Sitcom set in a charmingly dysfunctional police training college. B Group learn how to deal with missing persons and discover the crucial importance of the golden hour - meanwhile, two new recruits join the class in the form of the irrepressible Danni, who is soon to be married and will not let anyone forget it, and Connor, an enigmatic teller of very tall tales. Still struggling to knock the trainees into shape, Superintendents Bob Weekes and Julie Spry find themselves competing to accompany Chief Superintendent Cunningham to a conference in the Bahamas - elsewhere, Sergeant Daz Black is on a final warning about his violent conduct and must undergo anger management sessions as Julie assigns him to a course of therapy from the slightly under-qualified Melanie that makes him even angrier, and Student Officer Paul Huggins has been exposed as a mole (or 'prune in the nest') placed in the college by his criminal family and is now forced to work for the police as a 'double prune'.

programme.title: Law & Order: UK
programme.desc: Crime drama series about the two vital parts of the criminal justice system - the police who investigate crime and the Crown Prosecution Service who bring the offenders to trial. When Ronnie and Joe investigate the fatal stabbing of Dr Philip Gardner, a psychiatrist with a caseload of violent adolescent patients, their first instinct is to question the young people he was treating. Then evidence suggests that he may have been having an affair with one of them, and they begin to suspect the doctor's wife Alison. Although initially she denies killing her husband, Alison changes her defence as the case stacks up against her. Pleading that she was not in her right mind and lost control at the time of the stabbing, she makes a persuasive case. Her case is in fact so persuasive that Kate begins to question whether Alison should be on trial for murder at all, but Jake is determined to see justice done. Thanks to some last minute detective work, the team are finally able to uncover the truth.

programme.title: Law & Order: UK
programme.desc: Crime drama series. Ronnie and Joe come across a skeleton in a car boot at the bottom of the Thames. It turns out that the dead man was Taylor Kane, a black undercover police officer who went missing at the time of the Brixton riots in the 1980s. Unsettling evidence comes to light as Ronnie, Joe and Wes begin to raise issues and ask questions which the police would rather forget - and Wes gets an unexpected visit from the Commissioner. In court, Jake takes up the prosecution case as Philip Nevins appears for the defendant, DS Darren Grady. Accusations are thrown and the trial hits the headlines. Wes, Ronnie and Joe are drawn deeper and deeper into a case which sees the law itself in the witness box. Then Kane's sister Nikki comes knocking at their door. It is time to choose sides as friendships and loyalties are tested and careers are put on the line in the interests of justice.

programme.title: Trial & Retribution
programme.desc: The conclusion of this case of the crime drama. As the police begin their enquiry, prostitute Marilyn Spark is found half dead in an alleyway in Kings Cross - she has been badly beaten, sexually assaulted and had one of her breasts slashed. Marilyn's injuries are almost identical to Susan Harrow's - she is unable to speak, but she does manage to communicate to the police that she was attacked by one man and gives a description of him that includes the fact that he was wearing a red, blue and green-hooded sweater. Marilyn also describes a white van with distinctive markings across the rear doors - meanwhile, schoolteacher Carol Lennox is found murdered and her body dumped near a block of flats. Carol has been attacked in the same way as the other two, and when eyewitness Mehmet Al Said says that he also saw a white Nissan van in the vicinity, the evidence strongly suggests there is a common factor linking all three crimes.
